points.description: Let V, W be the incircle tangency points on AB, AC. Uses the tangency of EF to the incircle to show that the circumcircles of ABC, AVW and AEF concur at a second point P (other than A). Equivalent valid arguments earn the marks.

levels.says: States or sets up the concurrency of the circles with only partial or incomplete justification.

points.description: Uses P (or another valid route) to prove that Q, the second intersection of ray IH_0 with the circumcircle, is the tangency point of the A-mixtilinear incircle with the circumcircle. Hence Q = Y.

levels.says: Identifies Q with the mixtilinear tangency point but the justification has a significant gap.

points.description: Proves that K (the intersection of IO with BC) is the reflection of D across the midpoint M of BC.

levels.says: States this reflection property without a complete proof.

points.description: Concludes that X, Y, K are collinear, using the points above together with the definition of X as the second intersection of QD with the circumcircle. For example, shows that line QD meets the circumcircle again at a point on line YK, with a valid argument.

rubric.notes: Full marks need a complete proof covering the concurrency, the identification of Q with the mixtilinear tangency point, K as the reflection of D over M, and the final collinearity. Part marks go for the milestones in the grading guidelines, and equivalent methods are accepted. Claims with no proof earn at most half of a point.
